scope: targeted current-web stress test of stage-decomposition and retrieval-versus-use claims; not an exhaustive literature review

sources.title: Beyond Retrieval: Query-Conditioned Reuse of Long-Horizon Agent Trajectories
sources.collision: Explicitly separates retrieval from post-retrieval reuse and evaluates reuse while holding retrieval candidate, target state, model, decoding, and tool budget fixed.
sources.c1_boundary: C1 must not claim retrieval-versus-reuse separation itself as novel. The residual object is the same-trajectory reward-conditioned write intervention followed through native exposure, first-action uptake, and endpoint behavior, with forced capacity as a bypassed side control and ordinal localization.

sources.title: A Survey on Long-Term Memory Security in LLM Agents: Attacks, Defenses, and Governance Across the Memory Lifecycle
sources.collision: Organizes persistent memory into lifecycle phases including Write, Store, Retrieve, Execute, Share & Propagate, and Forget & Rollback.
sources.c1_boundary: C1 must not sell lifecycle partitioning or stage names as novelty. Its contribution must come from the controlled paired intervention, the evidence pattern, and the ordinal first-unsupported-stage localization.

demoted_novelty_claims: retrieval and post-retrieval use are distinct
agent memory should be decomposed into lifecycle stages
write/retrieve/execute stage naming is itself a new scientific object

surviving_residual.scientific_object: reward-conditioned same-trajectory persistent-state contrast and its stage-resolved native behavioral transport
surviving_residual.intervention: hold the source trajectory fixed and flip the success/failure writer branch
surviving_residual.side_control: forced fixed-evidence capacity control that bypasses native retrieval
surviving_residual.localization: ordinal first-unsupported-native-stage rule preserving stage-specific evidence semantics
surviving_residual.current_boundary: after exposure and before stable first-action uptake

manuscript_requirements: Related Work must cite QCR and explicitly disclaim retrieval-versus-reuse novelty.
Related Work must acknowledge prior memory-lifecycle decompositions and disclaim stage-naming novelty.
Introduction contribution must name the same-trajectory reward-conditioned intervention rather than generic stage decomposition.
No abstract/introduction claim may say or imply that C1 is the first work to distinguish retrieval from use.
